t: A planned city in the Valley of Mexico that grew to perhaps 100,000 people, among the largest in the world in the 3rd–6th centuries CE.
Its pyramids, obsidian, art and talud-tablero architecture influenced Mesoamerica as far as the Maya cities of Tikal and Copán.
No ruler is named in its art; around 550 its centre was burned, probably in a revolt, and the Aztecs later revered its ruins.
dyk: In 2003 archaeologists found a sealed tunnel about 100 metres long beneath the Feathered Serpent Pyramid, from which they later recovered tens of thousands of offerings and traces of liquid mercury.
ev: Teotihuacan begins to grow rapidly in the north-eastern Basin of Mexico
The Pyramid of the Sun is raised beside the Avenue of the Dead
The Feathered Serpent Pyramid is built, with some 200 sacrificial burials
The city covers some 20 km² with perhaps 100,000 inhabitants
Siyaj K’ak’ arrives at Tikal, and a new king linked to Teotihuacan takes power
K’inich Yax K’uk’ Mo’ founds the royal dynasty of Copán
The civic centre is burned and the city’s power collapses

f.predecessor: Formative-period villages of the Basin of Mexico
f.successor: Epiclassic centres such as Xochicalco, Cacaxtla and Cholula
